raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Python frontend reports `meta_info.cached_tokens` (prompt tokens served from the prefix cache) and `meta_info.reasoning_tokens` on every `/generate` frame, and usage accounting built on `/generate` reads cache hits from the first. The Rust frontend's `GenerateMetaInfo` carried neither, so a Rust-mode server reported no cache hits and no reasoning counts to its clients.

## Modifications

- The scheduler already counts both per request. In Rust mode the output streamer skipped them together with the fields only Python's detokenizer reads; it now records them for both frontends.
- The two counters ride the scheduler-to-Rust batch frame as two more core header columns after `tok_lens` (`BatchHeader` in `rust/sglang-server/src/message/response.rs` and `header_cols` in `python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py` change in lockstep). They are running totals, so each request's latest chunk value wins; `for_each_chunk` rejects a header whose new columns do not cover the batch, like the existing core columns.
- `GenerateMetaInfo` gains `cached_tokens` (uint32) and `reasoning_tokens` (uint64) in `proto/sglang/api/v1/generate.proto`. HTTP (unary, streaming, batch) and gRPC frames carry both on every frame, as the Python server does. The Rust and Python bindings are what `cargo gen-api` writes.
- Out of scope: OpenAI `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (`--enable-cache-report`) and the remaining Python-only `meta_info` fields (`cached_tokens_details`, `queue_time`, speculative-decoding stats, `weight_version`). #40258 proposes a wider set of these fields over a different header encoding; this change is the smallest one that gets the two usage counters onto the wire.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no model or numerics change).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: two scalar columns per request in the decode batch header. `ChunkEvent` stays within the `chunk_event_frame_stays_small` size budget.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` on the Python files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
  - `rust/`: `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server -p sglang-api-types` pass. The batch-frame decode test carries non-zero cache and reasoning columns and asserts them; the gRPC service test asserts `cached_tokens` on its frames; the hand-built test headers carry the two new columns; the generated-type contract test and the cross-language fixture (`json_parity.json`) carry both keys, with one case non-zero.
  - Python: `test/registered/unit/api/v1/test_parity.py` and `test/registered/unit/api/v1/test_json_contract.py` expect the two keys (33 passed, 21 subtests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The fields are documented in the proto.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
